Self-hosting · Homelab · Privacy

Leaving the cloud: a home server instead of Google, iCloud & co.

At home I run a Proxmox server with 15+ services. Here is which cloud services it replaces for me, what it costs – in time – and where you are better off staying in the cloud.

Serge Zabolotny · 2026-10-25

  • Self-Hosting
  • Homelab
  • Proxmox
  • Nextcloud
  • Immich
  • Jellyfin
  • Home Assistant
  • Datenschutz

Why run your own server?

Photos, documents, calendars, films: most of it sits with big cloud providers – convenient, but with subscription fees, someone else’s terms of use and no real control. My home server replaces a large part of it. As a developer I also learn what counts in operations: virtualization, containers, networking, backups and monitoring.

What you can replace

Cloud serviceSelf-hostedWhat for
Google Drive, iCloud, DropboxNextcloudSync and share files
Google Photos, iCloud PhotosImmichBack up and search photos and videos from your phone
Streaming for your own libraryJellyfin, Navidrome, Calibre-WebFilms, music and e-books from your own collection
Scanner apps and cloud filingPaperless-ngxScan documents, make them searchable with OCR, file them
Vendor smart-home cloudsHome Assistant, MQTTControl and automate devices locally
Cloud camerasFrigateStore and analyze camera footage locally
Per-device ad blockersAdGuardFilter ads and trackers network-wide
Monitoring SaaSUptime Kuma, GlancesKeep an eye on availability and load

Note: Jellyfin does not replace a streaming catalogue like Netflix. It only manages media you own yourself.

Where you are better off staying in the cloud

  • E-mail: I recommend not hosting it yourself. Deliverability and spam reputation cost more upkeep than they are worth.
  • Anything that must never go down: my products (MeisterMeld, PflegeOasis) do not run at home, but on rented servers in Germany.

What it really costs

  • Hardware: a used mini PC is enough. Mine is an HP EliteDesk 800 G3 Mini with 16 GB RAM running 15+ services.
  • Time: updates, backups and troubleshooting are now your job.
  • Responsibility: if the data is gone, there is no support desk. That is why backups come before everything else.

Rule of thumb: self-host what you do not want to lose or hand over – and only if you are willing to test your backups regularly.
